## Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on April 04, 2025, the area sown under the summer crops is 60.22 lakh ha as compared to 52.40 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Of this, area  of  31.98  lakh  ha  has  been  sown  under  rice  this  year  against  the  previous  year  area  of 27.33 lakh ha (increase of 4.65 lakh ha).
2. Rabi harvesting Status: As on 04.04.2025, 58.71 % of Rabi sown area has been harvested all over India. Approximately 91.00% area of Pulses mainly in Lathyrus (96%), Urdbean (94%), Kulthi (90%), Moongbean (89%); 69.40% area of Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals mainly in Jowar (95%); 87.02 % area of Oilseeds majorly in Rapeseed & Mustard (90%); 38.00% of Wheat and 32.93 % area of Rice has been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25.
3. Rabi Season Area Coverage : For Rabi horticulture crops ,  major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion - 12.53 lakh ha (9.73 lakh ha last year), Potato - 20.03 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato - 3.13 lakh ha (3.14 lakh ha last year).
4. Weather Update :
- a) Temperature: Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 2-4°C is likely over many parts of Northwest  India,  Maharashtra,  and  South  Peninsular  India,  and  by  2-3°C  over  Central India. East India is expected to see no significant change, and Gujarat may experience a 2°C rise during the next 2 days.

A fall in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C is expected over Northwest India, Maharashtra, South Peninsular India, and East India. Gujarat may see a 2-4°C fall while Central India is likely to remain largely unchanged.

- b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01- 07 April, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 31% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India:  -50%;  (ii)  Northwest  India:  -49%;  (iii)  Central  India:  -16%;  and  South  Peninsula: +98%.

An upper air Cyclonic Circulation lay over east Bihar and the trough runs from east Bihar to  east  Vidarbha  in  lower  tropospheric  levels.  The  north-south  trough  runs  from Marathwada  to  south  Tamil  Nadu  across  interior  Karnataka  in  lower  tropospheric level.

An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over South Interior Karnataka in lower tropospheric level.

Isolated to Scattered light/moderate rainfall accompanied with thunderstorm, lightning & gusty  winds  likely  over  Kerala  &  Mahe  on  07th;  Karnataka  on  07th  &  08th;  East  and Northeast  India  during  07th-10th  April.    Isolated  Hailstorm  likely  over  Bihar  on  09th April.

Heavy  rainfall  very  likely  at  isolated  places  over  Assam  &  Meghalaya  on  09th  &  10 th , April.

Heat wave conditions likely at isolated few pockets over Gujarat state, Madhya Pradesh Rajasthan, West Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi and Punjab during 07th-10th April.

## 5. Inputs Situation

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As on 03 rd  April 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 72.91 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 40% of total live storage capacity (182.37 BCM).The current year's storage is nearly 114 percent of last year's storage and 118 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during  the  corresponding  period.  The  overall  storage  position  is  better than  the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
- b) Groundwater Levels : Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014-2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024.
- c) Seeds  and  Fertilizers :  For  Rabi  2024-25,  certified  seed  availability  is  337.98  lakh  quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.
6. Pests & Diseases: Over all intensity of pests and disease remained below Economic Threshold Level (ETL) and no major pest incidence was recorded.

## Rainfall Forecast:

## 03 rd  April - 09th April 2025

-  Isolated  to  Scattered  light/moderate  rainfall  accompanied  with  thunderstorm, lightning & gusty winds (speed 40-50 kmph) likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal, Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam, Kerala & Mahe on 07th & 08th; Karnataka  during  07th  -09th;  East  and  Northeast  India  during  07th-11th  April. Isolated Hailstorm likely over Assam & Meghalaya, Bihar on 08th and Jharkhand on  09th  April.  Heavy  rainfall  very  likely  at  isolated  places  over  Tamil  Nadu, Kerala & Mahe on 07th & 08th and over Assam & Meghalaya on 08th April.
-  No significant weather likely over rest parts of the country during the week.

## 10 th  April - 16 th  April 2025

-  Under  the  influence  of  western  disturbances,  scattered  to  fairly  widespread rainfall/snowfall is likely over Western Himalayan Region during some days of the week and light rainfall along with thunder storm likely over parts of plains of northwest India during some days of the week.
-  Light/moderate scattered to fairly widespread rainfall along with thunderstorm are likely over northeast India & adjoining East India during some/many days of the week.
-  Light/moderate rainfall along with thunderstorm also likely over extreme south Peninsular India during some days of the week.
-  Overall, rainfall is likely to be normal to above normal over all the homogeneous regions of India during the week.

## Temperature Forecast :

## 03 rd  April - 09th April 2025

-  Gradual  rise  in  maximum  temperatures  by  2-4°C  likely  over  many  parts  of Northwest India, Maharashtra and South Peninsular India during next 4 days and fall by 2-3°C during subsequent 3 days.
-  Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over many parts of central India during next 4 days and no significant change during subsequent 3 days.
-  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over many parts of East India  during  next  2  days  and  fall  by  2-3°C  during  subsequent  3  days  and  no significant change during subsequent 2 days.
-  Rise  in  maximum temperatures by about 2°C likely over Gujarat during next 2 days and no significant change during subsequent 2 days and fall by 2-4°C during subsequent 3 days.

## 10 th  April - 16 th   April 2025

-  Maximum temperatures are likely to be above normal by 2-3°C over most parts of northwest India and northeast India; and by 2-4°C over most parts of East India; near normal over rest parts of the country.

## Heat Wave forecast :

## Week 1 (04 - 10 April)

-  Heatwave to severe heat wave likely over Gujarat and Rajasthan during 5 th  -9 th  April and heat wave over Madhya Pradesh during 7 th  -9 th  April and over South Punjab, Haryana and adjoining west Uttar Pradesh on 7 th  & 8 th  April.
-  Hot & humid weather is likely over Gujarat state during 03rd-09th and over Konkan & Goa during 05 th  - 09 th  April, 2025.

## Week 2 ( 11 - 17 April)

-  There  is  low  probability  of  heat  wave  conditions  over  north  Coastal  Andhra  Pradesh  and Odisha during some days of the week.

Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on April 04, 2025, the area sown under the summer crops is 60.22 lakh ha as compared to 52.40 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Of this, area  of  31.98  lakh  ha  has  been  sown  under  rice  this  year  against  the  previous  year  area  of 27.33 lakh ha (increase of 4.65 lakh ha).
2. Rabi harvesting Status: As on 04.04.2025, 58.71 % of Rabi sown area has been harvested all over India. Approximately 91.00% area of Pulses mainly in Lathyrus (96%), Urdbean (94%), Kulthi (90%), Moongbean (89%); 69.40% area of Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals mainly in Jowar (95%); 87.02 % area of Oilseeds majorly in Rapeseed & Mustard (90%); 38.00% of Wheat and 32.93 % area of Rice has been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25.
3. Rabi Season Area Coverage : For Rabi horticulture crops ,  major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion - 12.53 lakh ha (9.73 lakh ha last year), Potato - 20.03 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato - 3.13 lakh ha (3.14 lakh ha last year).
4. Weather Update :
- a) Temperature: Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 2-4°C is likely over many parts of Northwest  India,  Maharashtra,  and  South  Peninsular  India,  and  by  2-3°C  over  Central India. East India is expected to see no significant change, and Gujarat may experience a 2°C rise during the next 2 days.

A fall in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C is expected over Northwest India, Maharashtra, South Peninsular India, and East India. Gujarat may see a 2-4°C fall while Central India is likely to remain largely unchanged.

- b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01- 07 April, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 31% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India:  -50%;  (ii)  Northwest  India:  -49%;  (iii)  Central  India:  -16%;  and  South  Peninsula: +98%.

An upper air Cyclonic Circulation lay over east Bihar and the trough runs from east Bihar to  east  Vidarbha  in  lower  tropospheric  levels.  The  north-south  trough  runs  from Marathwada  to  south  Tamil  Nadu  across  interior  Karnataka  in  lower  tropospheric level.

An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over South Interior Karnataka in lower tropospheric level.

Isolated to Scattered light/moderate rainfall accompanied with thunderstorm, lightning & gusty  winds  likely  over  Kerala  &  Mahe  on  07th;  Karnataka  on  07th  &  08th;  East  and Northeast  India  during  07th-10th  April.    Isolated  Hailstorm  likely  over  Bihar  on  09th April.

Heavy  rainfall  very  likely  at  isolated  places  over  Assam  &  Meghalaya  on  09th  &  10 th , April.

Heat wave conditions likely at isolated few pockets over Gujarat state, Madhya Pradesh Rajasthan, West Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi and Punjab during 07th-10th April.
